meta: Edward H. Potthast's seaside study In the Surf, about 1910, from his summers on the New England coast.
about: Edward Potthast was born in Cincinnati and studied in Munich and Paris before going back to the United States, where he began spending summers on the New England coast. There he studied the carefree seaside activities of bathers and picnickers. He never married, but he was especially fond of painting young mothers with their children. This panel has In the Surf on the front and a beach study on the back.
credit_line: Gift of Virginia Rose Glidden and family and Mr. and Mrs. William H. Marlatt Fund

meta: A courtesan reads a letter from an admirer beside a poem about Komachi in Teisai Hokuba's screen of the early 1800s.
about: A courtesan pores over a letter from an admirer, and the poem beside her says it is past midnight and the lady is the legendary Amagoi Komachi. The museum explains that midnight was closing time in Yoshiwara, Edo's licensed brothel district, and that Amagoi, or Praying for Rain, Komachi was a ninth-century poet known for her verse and beauty. Ukiyo-e artists and poets added layers of meaning with imagery from classical literature. Teisai Hokuba painted the two-panel screen in the early 1800s.
credit_line: The Kelvin Smith Collection, given by Mrs. Kelvin Smith

meta: Customers crowd a busy bistro bar in Félix Vallotton's painting of about 1895.
about: The painting shows a crowded bistro full of eager customers. The museum says you can almost hear the loud chatter and the shouts of orders to the busy servers behind the counter. The men at the bar are all in jackets, with rosy cheeks and noses, perhaps from the cold outdoors set against the warmth of their drinks. Félix Vallotton painted it around 1895.
credit_line: Nancy F. and Joseph P. Keithley Collection Gift

meta: White hollyhocks by Ogata Kōrin, bought by Charles Lang Freer from the Paris dealer Siegfried Bing.
about: Charles Freer's admiration for the simplicity of Ogata Kōrin's paintings began in 1887 with his first purchase of Japanese art, a folding fan with an ink sketch of a crane's head, though the fan is no longer thought authentic. He went on to acquire many works by Kōrin and other Rinpa artists. He bought this painting of hollyhocks from the Paris dealer Siegfried Bing. Kōrin often painted the subject on gold-leaf screens. The leaves use a Rinpa technique, with ink or pigment pooled by brushing and details added in gold.

meta: Mary Holland Bacher, the painter's wife, in Otto H. Bacher's Impressionist portrait of 1891, an early picture of a woman and tennis.
about: Otto Bacher was the first artist from Cleveland to win international fame, and this portrait of his wife, Mary Holland Bacher, shows the Impressionist style he took up after studying in Paris in the late 1880s. The museum says its unusual subject reflects the rise of tennis, one of the few sports of the day in which women could take part without seeming unfeminine or coarse. Bacher painted it in 1891.

meta: Michelangelo's unfinished Manchester Madonna, with the Virgin, the Child and the young Saint John, about 1497, in the National Gallery.
about: The Manchester Madonna is an unfinished painting attributed to Michelangelo, one of three surviving panel paintings given to him, and dated to his first period in Rome. It came to public attention at the Art Treasures Exhibition in Manchester in 1857, which gave it its name. Doubts about the attribution lasted for much of the 19th and 20th centuries, but most scholars now agree. The Virgin has one breast bared, as if she has just nursed her son, and tries to hold a book away from him. Two angels read a scroll behind her.

meta: Francesco Giamberti, architect and musician, painted by Piero di Cosimo about 1485, now in the Rijksmuseum.
about: This oil on panel by Piero di Cosimo, made around 1485, is in the Rijksmuseum in Amsterdam. It shows Francesco Giamberti, who lived from about 1404 to 1482 and was an architect and musician. Wikipedia says the details in the background show the influence of Hugo van der Goes.

meta: Shepherds and their families are frightened by a line of angels in Abraham Daniëlsz. Hondius's Annunciation to the Shepherds, 1663.
about: In a landscape, shepherds and their families are startled by the appearance of a long line of angels in the sky. A tent with shepherds stands at the right, a cow in the middle and a farm at the left. Abraham Daniëlsz. Hondius painted it in 1663 as a pendant to another picture in the Rijksmuseum.

meta: Mars throws back the bed curtain on the sleeping Venus in Louis Jean François Lagrenée's allegory of peace, 1770.
about: In this gentle allegory of peace, Mars, the god of war, throws back the rich green bed curtains that frame the scene. As the drapery parts, morning light spills in to reveal the sleeping Venus. Louis Jean François Lagrenée painted Mars and Venus, Allegory of Peace in 1770, and it is in the Getty.

meta: A lone rider on a white horse gallops through a romantic landscape in Jean Achille Benouville's painting of 1846.
about: Dark trees and a turbulent sky bring a romantic mood to this classical, ideal landscape, in which a lone rider on a white horse gallops through a deep space. The composition is organized in three clear zones that recede from the path in the foreground to a lake or river in the middle ground and then to a distant rocky mountain and the sea. Jean Achille Benouville painted it in 1846.

meta: Peasants smoke in an Antwerp inn while a young man slumps against the wall, painted by David Teniers around 1640.
about: An older man and a younger man smoke tobacco in the foreground, and the younger one rests limply against the wall with his head lolling back, a sign that he has smoked too much. A standing man fills his pipe and watches him with amusement. The museum says tobacco was a novelty in the 1600s, thought to be medicinal and recommended for damp places such as Antwerp, where Teniers painted this. Moral opponents warned of its danger to health, which made it a good subject for Flemish artists.
credit_line: Gift of Mr. and Mrs. J. H. Wade

meta: George Fisher, a Pennsylvania lawyer who retired to Pineford Farm, painted by Raphaelle Peale about 1790.
about: George Fisher's father was a Quaker who founded the borough of Middletown, Pennsylvania, in 1755, on the east bank of the Susquehanna River nine miles below Harrisburg. Fisher passed the bar in 1787 and practiced law there until he retired to Pineford Farm in Middletown. He died at 87 and is buried in Harrisburg. Raphaelle Peale painted his portrait.

meta: A meadow with a few trees closed off by a fence, in Geo Poggenbeek's Orchard of 1873.
about: A meadow with a few trees is closed off at the back by a fence. Geo Poggenbeek painted the Orchard in 1873. Mr. and Mrs. Drucker-Fraser of Montreux gave it to the Rijksmuseum.

meta: A river winds between hills topped with castles in Jan Griffier's River View of about 1680.
about: A mountain landscape has a river winding between the hills, with castles on the hilltops. A few boats float at the lower left, and travelers use a mountain path at the right. Jan Griffier painted this River View, which the catalog dates to 1680.
